atoms.text: Rocco is afraid of the dark. He doesn’t like it when all his friends leave and he has to sleep all by himself. Frank Fox helps Rocco with his fear.

instruction.text: Read and follow along with Frank and Rocco’s conversation.
instruction.sound: ssml: Read and follow along with Frank and Rocco’s conversation. <break time='700ms'/> Rocco is hearing noises in the dark.

atoms.text: Rocco is hearing noises in the dark.

atoms.b: Rocco, you are looking a little afraid. Everything okay, friend?
atoms.sound: ssml: Rocco, you are looking a little afraid. Everything okay friend?<break time='500ms'/>

atoms.b: It’s so dark tonight. I keep hearing noises, and it scares me. I can’t fall asleep.
atoms.sound: ssml: It’s so dark tonight. I keep hearing noises, and it scares me. I can’t fall asleep.<break time='500ms'/>

atoms.b: I love the nighttime and can see very well in the dark. I can help you look for what made those sounds. Would that help you feel less afraid?
atoms.sound: ssml: I love the nighttime and can see very well in the dark. I can help you look for what made those sounds. Would that help you feel less afraid?<break time='500ms'/>

atoms.b: Yes, I think that would help!
atoms.sound: ssml: Yes, I think that would help!<break time='500ms'/>

atoms.b: Well, let’s check it out! Oh, hello there wee mousy! There’s nothing to be afraid of Rocco. Your neighbour is a little mouse looking for a soft place to sleep.

Your neighbour is a little mouse looking for a soft place to sleep.<break time='500ms'/>

atoms.b: Oh, thank you for looking Frank. It sounded like it would be so much bigger!
atoms.sound: ssml: Oh, thank you for looking Frank. It sounded like it would be so much bigger!<break time='500ms'/>

atoms.a: How does Rocco feel about the dark?

feedback.end: That’s right, Rocco is feeling afraid. He doesn’t like being alone in the dark. When it’s dark, it’s easier to imagine scary things.

atoms.text:
Rocco doesn’t seem to like being afraid, but fear is very important. Feeling fear can mean a lot of things: it can alert us to danger or mean that we are outside our comfort zones.

Sometimes, listening to your fear is the right thing to do. Other times, you can face your fear and learn that it’s not so scary after all.

instruction.text: Find different parts of Rocco to see how he and others can experience fear.

feedback.end: Eyes show fear very clearly. They are large and round, taking in what the threat might be. Some people’s eyebrows also go up, and the mouth can open.

When you’re afraid, your heart beats faster. It can almost feel like it will beat out of your chest! This can sometimes be almost painful. A fast heartbeat can make your face red and cause you to sweat.
An upset tummy can also happen when you are afraid. Your tummy can feel like it has sunk and is lower than usual.
Having a dry throat is also a normal feeling when you are afraid. Other people’s throats feel tight, and it can be hard to talk.
Some people’s legs feel weak when they’re scared, other people feel strong and even run away. Some people shake or shiver when they are afraid, and others even get goosebumps.

atoms.text:
It’s okay to be afraid sometimes – everybody is! Remember, although fear isn’t very nice to feel, it is there for a reason.

Try to learn about what you are afraid of, ask lots of questions and always ask for help if you need it – just like Rocco asked his friend Frank. Now that Rocco knows Frank is there, he can sleep!

atoms.a: Choose the child who is feeling scared.
